name: The Project Library
headline: Homegrown tools for community building in the modern age
aboutContent: The Project Library is a website for you and me.

posts.title: Launching the Beta site!
posts.content:
Since December 2025, I have been hard at work to creating the Project Library. It’s finally at the place where I can start to share, and I can’t wait to do so. This website and the services it provides are very near and dear to me, as it’s something I’ve had on my list for more than *10 years*! It's not done yet, this is just the beginning. It’s something I dreamed up while I was working in mental health care. I felt like there wasn’t a great way to connect on shared interest and hobbies, or to create unique mentorship and other relationships based on shared learning.

The fabric of our society absolutely depends on the connections we create and nurture. We are safer and have longer lifespans when we are connected to others. As a millennial, I had the unique opportunity to grow up without a smart phone and enter into the world of social media as a young person. I customized my MySpace, ranked my friends, and moved to Facebook like the rest of us in that time. The internet is a very different place now. On the big social media platforms, you are the product. Large corporations gather and sell your data to better target ads, they gamify the interfaces so you are quite literally addicted. That’s on purpose. 

People deserve to be able to create and share online without becoming hopelessly addicted, or worry that their data is being stolen just so you can find a recipe or see photos of your family. I created this online bulletin board, slow social media, and set of tools for community builders just like me because I think it should exist— plain and simple. 

So with all that said, take a look around and let me know how I can improve things! It means so much to me that you might try it out and give me the opportunity to make this a useful and meaningful place to spend some time, find something that inspires you, and then get offline.

All the best,

Laurel
